correctness.rationale: The exact complex Fourier symbol has real part minus Gamma. Elementary sine identities give an exact algebraic-trigonometric first-mode root; explicit low-mode bounds and summation by parts cover all remaining finite modes uniformly. The exact geometric-series formula gives a C^1-uniform midpoint expansion; the unique zero then has the stated M^{-1} and O(M^{-3}) corrections. The standalone finite verifier checks arithmetic examples, not infinitely many modes. No boundary nonlinear claim is made.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic spectral formulas do not themselves state that mode 1 uniformly dominates all other modes in a growing network, nor determine the unique crossing with O(M^-3) error. The new proof supplies those ingredients.

The accepted single claim also has a sharp integer stability dichotomy, a proved uniform gap for all other growing modes and two explicit finite-size corrections. These are the assessed difference.

value.rationale: The third twisted family is a motivated first unresolved higher-winding case after a complete q=2 classification. It receives a genuinely sharp all-mode finite-network threshold rather than a continuum-only or sufficient range. An exact half-neighbor correction and nonzero next coefficient quantify the finite-population connectivity budget, a documented source of misclassification, with transparent limits.
